notes: Shows that the dynamical architecture of a motor pattern generator determines how it uses sensory feedback: a nominal Aplysia swallowing model tuned near a heteroclinic channel (versus a generic limit cycle) reproduces in vivo load-induced motor changes and the dramatic slowing seen in vitro when proprioceptive feedback is removed, and matches in vivo burst-length distributions better. Argues that limit-cycle CPG models can miss key load-adaptive properties, so architecture choice constrains how sensory feedback shapes rhythm timing.
animal_study: Replicate the regime-classification approach in another rhythmic system: measure burst-length distributions and responses to added load and to graded proprioceptive removal, then test whether the data favor heteroclinic-channel over limit-cycle dynamics as demonstrated for Aplysia in vitro.
robot_sim: Implement two CPG variants that differ only in architecture (limit cycle vs heteroclinic channel) in a neuromechanical simulation with load-dependent sensory input; compare their responses to load perturbations and to sensory ablation, checking for the predicted slowing and burst-length distribution changes.
flags: Animal is Aplysia (mollusc), absent from the animals vocabulary; the load/proprioceptive-modulation pathway has no feedback vocabulary entry.

notes: Bilateral hindpaw cutaneous denervation at the ankle in intact cats barely disrupts level treadmill walking but severely impairs ladder and incline walking early on; flexor EMG remains permanently elevated and mediolateral ground reaction forces increase by 200 percent, showing cutaneous feedback matters most for demanding locomotor contexts and that active adaptive mechanisms compensate without fully restoring the control pattern. The companion paper shows these same inputs become critical for foot placement after spinalization.
animal_study: Combine graded cutaneous denervation with spinalization in the same animals to quantify when cutaneous input shifts from contributory to critical for foot placement, and track EMG compensation chronologically to dissect the adaptive mechanisms.
robot_sim: Add foot/ankle cutaneous afferent channels to a walking simulation and ablate them: the model should reproduce near-normal level walking with degraded ladder/incline behavior, persistently elevated flexor drive, and increased mediolateral ground reaction forces.

notes: Argues from convergent evolution that insects and vertebrates independently arrived at similar neural control properties and mechanical schemes for legged locomotion, highlighting leg specialization, body flexion, and complex head-mounted sensing as critical for complex-terrain agility - features most robots of the era lacked. The design-transfer principle is selection rather than copying: pick the properties critical for the target behavior when building a robot.
animal_study: Quantify the convergent properties experimentally, for example measure how restricting body flexion or ablating leg specialization changes complex-terrain traversal in insects, testing whether the convergent features are functionally critical as the convergent-evolution argument predicts.
robot_sim: Build legged-robot models that incrementally add leg specialization, body flexion, and head-region sensing over a homogeneous-leg rigid-body baseline, and compare complex-terrain agility to test which convergent properties carry the performance benefit.

notes: First in vivo demonstration of a neuromorphic silicon CPG replacing central nervous system function: a chip of ten integrate-and-fire silicon neurons with 190 programmable synapses drove the motor output of a paralyzed animal to walk a three-meter platform in real time, under closed-loop control using sensory feedback recorded from the animal's legs. Establishes that compact neuromorphic hardware with biological-style sensory feedback can suffice for locomotor pattern generation in a living preparation.
animal_study: The paradigm itself seeds animal studies: run the paralyzed-animal preparation with the silicon CPG open-loop versus closed-loop (leg sensory feedback on/off) and across different synaptic configurations to identify which circuit properties and feedback channels are necessary for overground walking.
robot_sim: Emulate the chip architecture in software (ten integrate-and-fire neurons, arbitrary programmable connectivity, tonic bias, external inputs closed-loop with leg sensory signals) and ablate the sensory feedback path to quantify its contribution to walking stability.
flags: Abstract does not state the animal species or afferent types (only 'sensory feedback recorded from the animal's legs'); no feedback vocabulary match for closed-loop neuromorphic sensory input.

notes: In unrestrained walking cats, cutaneous stimulation evokes phase-modulated responses: two excitatory peaks (about 10 and 25 ms) in flexors that grow toward the end of stance, early inhibition then late excitation (P3, about 35 ms) in extensors when stimuli fall in early stance, and crossed responses in the contralateral limb at 20-25 ms. Concludes the walking cat shows modulation of transmission in a flexor-excitatory/extensor-inhibitory pathway - likely by the flexor part of the spinal locomotor oscillator - rather than strict reflex reversal, plus specialized flexor-inhibitory and extensor-excitatory routes.
animal_study: Record from spinal interneurons during phase-modulated cutaneous reflexes in walking cats to locate where the locomotor oscillator gates transmission, and compare sural versus plantar stimulation sites to map the specialized flexor-inhibitory and extensor-excitatory pathways.
robot_sim: Implement cutaneous reflex pathways with locomotor-phase gating: flexor excitation whose gain peaks at late stance, extensor inhibition during early stance, and crossed extensor/flexor responses; ablating the phase gating tests the oscillator-modulation hypothesis versus fixed reflex reversal.

notes: A 3D neuro-musculo-mechanical salamander model shows proprioceptive feedback - girdle stretch-receptor-like intraspinal neurons plus hip and scapula limb stretch receptors - is essential for a coordinated lateral-sequence walking gait, while walking trot is dominated by the CPG; the walk-to-trot transition can be induced by increased descending drive from the mesencephalic locomotor region and is helped by hip/scapula sensory input signaling late stance. Demonstrates that the sensory-versus-central balance of control differs by gait.
animal_study: The authors' own call: identify the mechanoreceptor types and modulation mechanisms in the salamander girdles and limbs electrophysiologically, and test the gait-transition prediction by stimulating the mesencephalic locomotor region while selectively blocking hip/scapula stretch-receptor input.
robot_sim: Implement girdle and hip/scapula stretch-receptor feedback onto a body-CPG plus four limb-CPGs network in simulation; ablate the sensory modulation to check that lateral-sequence walking degrades while trot survives, and gate the walk-to-trot switch on late-stance stretch detection with increasing descending drive.
flags: Feedback pathway (late-stance stretch-receptor input aiding gait transition and essential for walking coordination) has no vocabulary entry - stretch receptors are not typed as Ia/II in the abstract.

notes: Shows that analytically designed, biologically constrained neural controllers for bipedal balance can reproduce classical inverted-pendulum control behavior, with each neural parameter correlated to a classical control parameter: varying neural parameters changes system dynamics as classical theory predicts. Establishes a porting recipe from classical control models to compact dynamic neural architectures.
animal_study: Test the parameter-to-stability mappings in human balance experiments: perturb stance and manipulate task demands, then check whether observed adaptation matches the changes predicted when the corresponding neural parameters are varied.
robot_sim: Use the analytical design method to port a classical bipedal balance controller to a neural network in simulation, then ablate or perturb individual neural parameters to verify each reproduces the dynamics change its correlated classical parameter predicts.

notes: Review establishing that spinal networks generate the basic locomotor rhythm across vertebrates including man, with limb sensory feedback essential for effective locomotion: sensory regulation reaches motoneurons via reflex pathways that bypass the rhythm generators and also acts on the locomotor networks themselves, controlling phase timing, shaping muscle-activity patterns, adding excitatory drive, and driving long-term adaptation - the basis for treadmill-training rehabilitation after spinal cord injury.
animal_study: In spinalized preparations or spinal-cord-injury patients, dissociate the two sensory routes by stimulating limb afferents during treadmill locomotion and measuring phase-timing versus pattern changes, testing whether reflex-bypass and CPG-directed pathways can be selectively engaged for rehabilitation.
robot_sim: Implement both sensory routes in a locomotion model - direct reflex pathways to motoneurons plus afferent input to the rhythm generator - and ablate each separately to test their predicted contributions to phase timing, pattern shaping, and net excitatory drive.

notes: Frames postural control as two interacting goals - orientation (active alignment of trunk and head to gravity, support surface, and visual surround) and equilibrium (movement strategies stabilizing the center of body mass) - achieved by dynamic sensorimotor processes in which the weighting of somatosensory, vestibular, and visual inputs depends on task goals and context; anticipatory postural adjustments precede voluntary limb movement, and damage to different underlying systems yields context-specific instabilities.
animal_study: Test context-specific instability predictions by selectively disrupting individual sensory systems (visual, vestibular, somatosensory) or CNS subsystems during stance and perturbation tasks, mapping which postural goal and response strategy degrades for each lesion.
robot_sim: Implement a balance controller with task- and context-dependent weighting of somatosensory, vestibular, and visual channels plus anticipatory postural adjustments before limb movements; ablating single channels should reproduce distinct, context-specific instability signatures.

notes: Observer-design analysis of canonic neural oscillator models (Hodgkin-Huxley, Hindmarsh-Rose, FitzHugh-Nagumo, Morris-Lecar): they are locally observable but not in adaptive observer canonic form, and no parameter-independent diffeomorphism converts them; parameter-dependent transformations nevertheless allow partial state/parameter reconstruction with exponential convergence, and a Lyapunov plus positive-invariance/small-gain method handles nonlinearly entering parameters while avoiding ill-conditioning and non-uniqueness.
robot_sim: Apply these observers to estimate hidden states and parameters of neural oscillator/CPG models in real time from sparse outputs (a few state components plus the input signal), enabling online identification and tuning of simulated CPGs and model-based decoding for closed-loop neural control.

notes: Robot fish driven by a CPG of four neural oscillators with sensory feedback from three infrared sensors and a gyro; two feedback strategies mapped to CPG model parameters control pitching and turning respectively, with simulations validating rhythm generation for pectoral-fin and tail-flapping locomotion. An early engineering demonstration that modulating CPG parameters with simple exteroceptive and proprioceptive signals suffices for posture and heading control in swimming.
robot_sim: Reproduce the two feedback strategies in a simulated swimmer: map obstacle-detection (infrared-analog) and posture (gyro-analog) signals onto CPG parameters for turning and pitching, then ablate each feedback path to quantify the open- versus closed-loop difference in obstacle avoidance and attitude stability.

notes: Males show less extensibility and greater active and passive knee-flexor stiffness than females, measured by final knee position in active extension, the slope of the passive moment-angle curve, and damping of imposed vibratory motion under 10 percent body-mass loading; the sex differences may be functions of greater male mass and height, with relevance to higher female anterior cruciate ligament injury rates.
robot_sim: Use the measured passive and active knee-flexor stiffness values (and their sex differences) as joint-level stiffness parameters in a neuromuscular knee model, testing whether stiffness differences alone - without altered reflex gains - change joint stability margins.
flags: Marginal for a sensory-afferent database: biomechanical stiffness comparison with no afferent or reflex pathway content in the abstract.

notes: Review of walking restoration after spinal cord injury: treadmill training with partial weight support exploits spinal locomotor networks whose training-induced improvement mechanisms were revealed in animal studies; functional electrical stimulation of nerves and muscles assists stepping; and regeneration strategies promote growth of damaged axons - but no direct spinal-cord treatment is in routine use, so successful protocols will likely combine re-establishing functional connections to spinal networks with task-specific rehabilitation that shapes their motor patterns.
animal_study: In animals with damaged spinal cords, test the combination the review proposes: pair a regeneration-promoting treatment with task-specific locomotor training and measure whether stepping patterns are shaped beyond what either intervention alone produces.
robot_sim: Model spinal locomotor networks with training-induced plasticity and FES-like activation: simulate reconnection plus task-specific shaping signals and test whether the combination, not either alone, recovers stepping, including which feedback channels the training exploits.

notes: A conductance-based model built from the mean maximal conductances of a population of equivalent one-spike bursters fires three action potentials per burst instead of one, because the population occupies a highly concave region of parameter space that does not contain its mean - demonstrating that averaging parameters across multiple preparations can fail to characterize a system whose behavior depends on interactions among highly variable components. A core caution for parameterizing neural models from pooled experimental data.
animal_study: Measure maximal-conductance variability across identified neurons in multiple preparations and test whether behavior correlates with parameter covariation across the population rather than with any single-parameter mean, as the concave-parameter-space argument predicts.
robot_sim: When fitting neural or CPG models to multiple experimental recordings, select parameter sets by matching behavior rather than by averaging parameters, and always verify that the mean-parameter model reproduces the target dynamics - an explicit modeling-hygiene rule for database-driven model construction.

notes: Book chapter synthesizing sensory control of posture and locomotion in arthropods and vertebrates through classical feedback-control theory, arguing that experimental paradigms, reduced animal preparations, and neuromechanical modeling must be combined to understand postural control, which in both groups maintains a body-configuration set point (a set of joint angles keeping the body above the feet) during standing, locomotion, and other movements, and resists sudden perturbations.
animal_study: Apply perturbation paradigms in reduced arthropod and vertebrate preparations to isolate individual sensory feedback loops, testing the control-theoretic prediction that each loop defends a defined body-configuration variable against disturbances.
robot_sim: Build posture controllers for simulated walkers per the chapter's framework - body-configuration set points defended by sensory feedback loops - and ablate loops individually to compare predicted versus resulting postural deficits in arthropod- and vertebrate-style morphologies.

notes: Historical review of Eccles' intracellular recordings defining five classical spinal reflex systems - recurrent inhibition of motoneurons via motor axon collaterals and Renshaw cells, pathways from muscle spindles and Golgi tendon organs, presynaptic inhibition, and the flexor reflex - and of Lundberg's demonstration that spinal interneurons converge segmental sensory afferents with descending pathways, the keystone for modern hypotheses of spinal motor control later tested in behaving animals and non-invasively in humans.
animal_study: Directly record genetically identified spinal interneurons in behaving animals during natural movements to test the functional roles of the Eccles-Lundberg reflex circuits, and examine plasticity of these pathways during motor learning and neurorehabilitation.
robot_sim: Implement the classical circuit library - Renshaw recurrent inhibition, spindle and tendon-organ reflex pathways, presynaptic inhibition, flexor reflex - as separable modules in a spinal network model, ablating each to quantify its contribution to motor output.
flags: Renshaw recurrent inhibition and (untyped) presynaptic inhibition are core topics but absent from the feedback vocabulary; afferents inferred as Ia/II/Ib from 'muscle spindles and Golgi tendon organs' in the abstract.

notes: Reassesses the subdivision of adult mammalian spinal intermediate-zone interneurons and finds no compelling reason to separate those with group Ib input from those co-excited by group II afferents: distributed input patterns, projection targets (ipsilateral, contralateral, bilateral), excitatory versus inhibitory identity, and task-dependent reflex changes during locomotion are all consistent with shared premotor interneurons integrating group I and II signals - prompting the proposed renaming to group I/II interneurons.
animal_study: Record identified intermediate-zone interneurons during locomotion and test whether individual neurons integrate convergent group I and II input with task-dependent output changes, the key prediction of the merged group I/II population proposal.
robot_sim: Replace separate Ib and II reflex channels in a locomotion model with a single premotor interneuron population receiving convergent group I and II input, and test whether the merged population reproduces the task-dependent reflex modulation and reversals seen during locomotion.
flags: Core claim - shared group I/II premotor integration rather than separate Ib and II populations - has no feedback vocabulary entry.

notes: In chronic spinal cats walking on a treadmill, a limb held by the paw lifts off and rejoins walking once the hip is brought far enough back, at a hip angle very close to that of normal swing initiation, and lift-off also tends to occur at particular contralateral cycle phases. Establishes hip position and contralateral step-cycle phase as two key factors determining swing initiation, i.e., the stance-to-swing transition is regulated by proprioceptive and interlimb signals rather than a fixed internal clock.
animal_study: Block or manipulate hip-joint afferent signals during locomotion in spinal cats and mechanically vary the contralateral cycle phase to dissociate the two swing-initiation factors, testing whether either alone suffices to trigger lift-off.
robot_sim: Implement swing initiation in a walking model as a hip-extension position threshold gated by contralateral cycle phase; ablating the hip-position input should delay or prevent swing onset, reproducing the held-paw behavior.
flags: Abstract names no afferent type for the hip-position signal (the vocabulary item 'Ia or II stance to swing' would require that assumption); the contralateral-phase gating also has no vocabulary entry.

notes: In two chronic stroke patients, 18 sessions of treadmill gait training augmented with continuous real-time visual feedback (immersive virtual environment) and proprioceptive feedback (dual-belt treadmill) improved gait speed and spatiotemporal symmetry beyond levels previously reported, with each patient improving the symmetry dimension they trained (step-length versus stance-time). Shows augmented sensory channels can drive relearning of gait symmetry after stroke.
animal_study: Test combined visual and proprioceptive symmetry feedback in a larger stroke cohort with retention follow-up, and dissociate the two channels to determine whether proprioceptive (split-belt driven) or visual augmentation drives the symmetry gains.
robot_sim: Model gait adaptation as an external feedback loop: real-time symmetry error signals delivered through visual and proprioceptive channels drive step-to-step correction of a neuromuscular gait controller, reproducing the differential improvement in the trained symmetry dimension.

notes: Review showing that in mammals with complete spinal cord injury, somatosensory input from the lumbar region powerfully inhibits hindlimb locomotion while perineal input facilitates it, and the two regions oppositely regulate cutaneous reflexes from the foot (lumbar input increases reflex gain, perineal input decreases it); spinal cord injury can also cause loss of functional specificity, with somatosensory feedback abnormally co-activating functions such as locomotion and micturition.
animal_study: In spinalized cats, stimulate lumbar versus perineal regions during locomotion while recording locomotor output and foot cutaneous reflexes, testing the opposite inhibitory/facilitatory CPG effects and reflex-gain modulation, and probing for pathological loss of functional specificity.
robot_sim: Add region-specific somatosensory gating to a spinal locomotor model: lumbar input inhibits and perineal input facilitates the CPG, with opposite modulation of cutaneous reflex gain; simulating complete spinal-cord injury then tests emergence of maladaptive co-activation of locomotion with other spinal functions.
flags: Lumbar-region (inhibitory) versus perineal (facilitatory) somatosensory modulation of the CPG and reflex gain has no feedback vocabulary entry.

notes: Fate-mapping shows mouse V1-derived interneurons develop into ipsilaterally projecting inhibitory cells (over 80 percent glycinergic varicosities, a third GABAergic, none glutamatergic or cholinergic) comprising Renshaw cells (9 percent), parvalbumin-only group 4 proprioceptive interneurons contacted by primary sensory afferents (27 percent), and a ventral subgroup resembling Ia inhibitory interneurons that receives convergent Renshaw cell input (13 percent); V1 axons never cross the midline.
animal_study: Silence or ablate specific V1-derived subgroups (Renshaw cells versus group 4 proprioceptive interneurons versus IaIN-like cells) in mice and measure the resulting reflex and locomotor changes to assign function to each developmental class.
robot_sim: Constrain spinal reflex circuitry in models so Renshaw cells, Ia inhibitory interneurons, and other proprioceptive interneurons derive from one ipsilateral inhibitory V1 lineage with convergent Renshaw-to-IaIN connections; ablating the lineage predicts which reflex components fail together.

notes: A phenomenological model of insect campaniform sensilla predicts afferent discharge as proportional to instantaneous stimulus force relative to an adaptive variable: nonlinear first-order dynamics reproduce power-law adaptation, rate sensitivity, and hysteresis as manifestations of a single mechanism, generalize across cockroach and stick insect sensillum groups after tuning to one response, and can be inverted to estimate stimulus force from recorded discharge - a compact transducer law for load feedback during walking.
animal_study: Record campaniform sensillum afferents during imposed force ramps, steps, and cyclic loads and test the model's predictions - single-response tuning generalizing to all stimuli and the shared adaptive-variable origin of adaptation, rate sensitivity, and hysteresis - and validate the inverted force estimation against measured loads.
robot_sim: Use the adaptive-variable campaniform model as the force-feedback transducer in a walking simulation or robot leg, and ablate the adaptive variable to test how tonic-force adaptation, rate sensitivity, and hysteresis each shape load-dependent motor control.
flags: The feedback vocabulary has only the trochanteral CS-to-MN item; this paper is a force-encoding transducer model without a specified central pathway, so feedback left empty.

notes: Perspective on linking spinal interneuron identity to locomotor function: molecular identification of broad interneuronal classes advanced the field, and adding location, electrophysiological properties, and connectivity sharpens function assignment, but some functional populations - notably rhythm-generating neurons - lack clear identifiers, and experience-dependent plasticity plus spinal cord injury complicate subtype definitions, making multimodal classification necessary for understanding circuit function and dysfunction.
animal_study: Combine gene profiling with location, electrophysiology, connectivity, and perturbation recordings in behaving animals to assign function to molecularly defined spinal subtypes, and search for markers that uniquely identify rhythm-generating neurons.
robot_sim: Build locomotor network models whose unit classes are constrained by the multimodal classifiers, including an as-yet-unidentified rhythm-generating population; deleting specific classified subtypes in the model tests predicted functional deficits and can guide which neurons to target for identification.

notes: Continuous tendon vibration during blindfolded walking enhanced the EMG of quadriceps femoris and biceps femoris (mainly in stance) and quadriceps vibration advanced the onset of tibialis anterior within the gait cycle, while vibration of ankle and hip muscles had no significant amplitude effect - implicating Ia afferent input in stance-phase muscle activation and in a limited role in triggering phase transitions (stance to swing) during human locomotion.
animal_study: Localize the phase-transition effect spinal-versus-supraspinal: apply tendon vibration in spinal-cord-injured persons or under pharmacologically altered reflex states, and combine vibration with hip-joint positioning to test whether the Ia timing signal interacts with hip-position gating of swing initiation.
robot_sim: Implement Ia input as an amplitude contribution to stance-phase muscle activation plus a weak phase-transition trigger term driven by knee-extensor Ia activity; ablating the timing term should remove the advanced dorsiflexor onset while leaving the stance EMG enhancement intact.
